Here is a comprehensive overview of the **Men's Ski Cross** event at the **2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics**, based on official Olympic and FIS records, reputable sports journalism, and historical competition data.

### 📅 Event Details
- **Dates:** February 21, 2018 (Qualification & Finals held on the same day)
- **Venue:** Bokwang Phoenix Park (also referred to as Phoenix Snow Park), PyeongChang, South Korea
- **Discipline:** Freestyle Skiing – Ski Cross
- **Number of Competitors:** 32 athletes from 15 nations
- **Course:** ~950 meters long, featuring a steep start ramp, banked turns (berms), rollers, table-top jumps, and a technical finishing straight. Conditions were cold but clear, with no weather-related delays.

### 🏁 Competition Format
Ski cross uses a hybrid time-trial + head-to-head knockout format:
1. **Qualification:** Each skier completed a solo timed run. Times determined seeding for the knockout bracket.
2. **Knockout Rounds:** Heats of 4 skiers raced simultaneously. The top 2 finishers in each heat advanced.
3. **Bracket Progression:** Round of 32 → Round of 16 → Quarterfinals → Semifinals
4. **Finals:** 
   - **Big Final:** 1st–4th places (medals decided here)
   - **Small Final:** 5th–8th places
5. **Rules:** Incidental contact is allowed, but deliberate interference, blocking, or unsafe maneuvers can lead to disqualification via video review.

### 🥇 Medalists & Final Results
| Place | Athlete | Country | Note |
|-------|----------------------------|------|
| 🥇 Gold | **Brady Leman** | Canada | First Olympic men's ski cross gold for Canada |
| 🥈 Silver | **Marc Bischofberger** | Switzerland | Career-best Olympic result |
| 🥉 Bronze | **Sergey Ridzik** | Olympic Athletes from Russia (OAR) | Recovered from a late crash to secure bronze |
| 4th | Victor Öhling Norberg | Sweden | Fell on the final turn, finished 4th |

*(Note: Russian athletes competed under the "Olympic Athletes from Russia" designation due to IOC sanctions on the Russian Olympic Committee.)*

### 🔍 Key Moments & Highlights
- **Brady Leman's Victory:** Leman, who had struggled with injuries and near-misses in previous Olympic cycles, executed a near-flawless final. He grabbed the holeshot (first into the first turn) and controlled the pace throughout, never relinquishing the lead.
- **Sergey Ridzik's Dramatic Bronze:** In the big final, Ridzik was running third when he caught an edge on the final banked turn and crashed. He quickly scrambled to his feet and crossed the line third, holding off a charging Öhling Norberg who also fell on the same feature. The moment became one of the most replayed clips of the Games.
- **End of French Dominance:** France had swept the podium in Sochi 2014 (Chapuis, Bovolenta, Midol). In PyeongChang, defending champion Jean-Frédéric Chapuis was eliminated in the quarterfinals, and no French skier reached the big final.
- **Video Review Use:** Several heats featured jury reviews for alleged blocking or dangerous line changes, consistent with FIS's increased emphasis on safety and fair racing after controversies in earlier World Cup seasons.

### 🌍 Historical Context & Significance
- **Olympic History:** Ski cross made its Olympic debut at Vancouver 2010. PyeongChang 2018 marked its third appearance.
- **Canadian Dominance:** Leman's gold came one day before Canada's women swept ski cross (Kelsey Serwa gold, Brittany Phelan silver), marking the first time a single nation won both men's and women's Olympic ski cross titles at the same Games.
- **Leman's Career Arc:** Brady Leman had been a consistent World Cup contender but carried the weight of a DNF in the 2014 Sochi quarterfinals. His 2018 gold was widely viewed as a redemption story and cemented his legacy in Canadian freestyle skiing.
- **OAR Participation:** Ridzik's bronze was one of several medals won by Russian athletes competing neutrally. The IOC allowed clean athletes to participate under strict conditions, and Ridzik's result stood without controversy.

### 📊 Participation & Notable Entrants
- **Top Nations Represented:** Canada, Switzerland, France, Germany, Austria, Sweden, USA, OAR, Japan, Australia
- **Defending Champion:** Jean-Frédéric Chapuis (FRA) – eliminated in quarterfinals
- **World Champion (2017):** Victor Öhling Norberg (SWE) – reached big final, finished 4th
- **Oldest Competitor:** Thomas Zangerl (AUT, born 1988)
- **Youngest Competitor:** Ryo Sugai (JPN, born 1998)

### 📚 Official Records & Further Reading
For heat-by-heat results, split times, course maps, and official jury decisions, you can consult:
- **Official PyeongChang 2018 Results Book:** [https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/pyeongchang-2018/results/freestyle-skiing/men-s-ski-cross](https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/pyeongchang-2018/results/freestyle-skiing/men-s-ski-cross)
- **FIS Freestyle Ski Cross Archive:** [https://www.fis-ski.com/](https://www.fis-ski.com/)
- **Olympic Channel Documentary/Highlights:** Search "PyeongChang 2018 Men's Ski Cross Final" for full race footage and post-race interviews.
